title: Prefix-free encoding condition
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type and let $f$ map each element of $\alpha$ to a finite Boolean word. The encoding satisfies the prefix-free condition if, for all $a,b\in\alpha$ and Boolean words $s,t$, equality $f(a)s=f(b)t$ under concatenation implies both $a=b$ and $s=t$.
